analysis:
1. What is given. The comment-stripped Verilog of every module in one file (aes_128, expand_key_128, one_round, final_round, table_lookup, S4, T, S, xS), each line prefixed with its line number, and a relationship map of their elements, records and flow graph; nothing else.
3. Purpose and use-case flows. aes_128 reads a block (state) and a key, XORs them into s0 and copies key into k0 on each rising edge of clk (lines 9, 11, 12), expands the key through the stages a1-a10 (lines 15-24), passes the block through the rounds r1-r9 (lines 26-34) and the final round rf (line 36), and drives rf's result on out. Every flow is an operate flow. F1, initial mixing: the input block XORed with the key, and the key itself, captured on the clock edge (lines 9, 11, 12). F2, key expansion in expand_key_128: the incoming stage key is split into words (line 48), mixed with the stage constant and chained (lines 49-52), registered (line 54), mixed with a substituted word (lines 56-60), and leaves as the next stage's key, registered (line 62), and as a round key (line 63). F3, a round in one_round: the block is split and looked up (lines 77, 79-82), XORed with the round key (lines 76, 83-86) and registered as the next block by `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` (line 88). F4, final round: the block is substituted (lines 103, 105-108), XORed with the last round key (lines 102, 109-112), registered (line 114) and driven out of aes_128 through `rf (clk, s9, k9b, out);` (line 36). F5, stage chaining in aes_128: each expansion stage's outputs feed the next stage and a round, and each round's output feeds the next round (lines 15-36). No configure, start, report, read-out, lock or reset flow is reported: the RTL has no held setting, request, status, lock or reset arm.
4. Flow graph. The only elements that drive SEQUENCES are the clk inputs, and nothing drives RESETS. PATH key (aes_128) reaches the stores k0 and s0 and the connections a1.in and r1.state_in; PATH state reaches s0 and r1.state_in. In expand_key_128, PATH in reaches the stores k0a-k3a, the exits out_1 and out_2 and the connection S4_0.in. In the rounds, PATH key (one_round) and PATH key_in (final_round) reach state_out, while PATH state_in ends at the lookup connections t0-t3.state and S4_1-S4_4.in: the substitution happens in sub-units, and its results come back on the p words that lines 83-86 and 109-112 recombine. PATH state (table_lookup) reaches only the connections t0-t3.in. No PATH reaches out of aes_128: its only record is the connection from rf.state_out (occurrence 3, line 36). There is no CONTROL-ONLY source, and nothing gates or selects on these paths; the only selectors are the `case (in)` statements inside S and xS (lines 154, 418), within the substitution units.
5. Established values. Key material: F1-F5 depend on it. Integrity: `s0 <= state ^ key;` (line 11), the capture `k0 <= key;` (line 12), the expansion at line 49 and the round mixing at lines 83 and 109 become wrong if it changes. Availability: `out_1 <= {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` (line 62) delivers the next stage's key on every rising edge (line 61). Intermediate state: F1, F3 and F5 depend on it. Integrity: `assign z0 = p00 ^ p11 ^ p22 ^ p33 ^ k0;` (line 83), whose registered result each next round reads (lines 26-36). Availability: the next block is registered at each rising edge (lines 87-88). Finished block: F4 depends on it. Integrity: `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109) and lines 110-112. Availability: registered at line 114 on the edge of line 113 and delivered on out through line 36, without assuming an external deadline. All three are Established on integrity, which the serialization rule selects. Confidentiality is context-dependent and not claimed: no line restricts who observes key, k0, out_1, out_2 or out, and calling the key secret is not a line. The input block before key mixing (state) and the stage constant rcon are distinct values; this example develops only the concepts above.
6. Roles along the path. Key material: key (aes_128) sets, occurrence 4, CARRIES to k0 (line 12; it also SOURCES s0 at line 11), read here to be stored; k0 (aes_128) stores, occurrence 2, CLOCKED_BY clk (line 12), an unchanged capture that still stores; in (expand_key_128) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k1 (line 48; the record targets k0-k3), and its words feed the local expansion (lines 49-52), so it is not unchanged forwarding; out_1 exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM k0b (line 62), exit ahead of its storage (CLOCKED_BY at the same line); out_2 exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM k0b (line 63); key (one_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k2 (line 76), used at line 85; key_in (final_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k3 (line 102), used at line 112. Not realizing it: the words k1 of expand_key_128, k2 of one_round and k3 of final_round, like the other words of each split, only carry a slice of their port (DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 2, lines 48, 76, 102); in aes_128, k1 connects a1.out_1 to a2.in, k0b connects a1.out_2 to r1.key and k9b connects a10.out_2 to rf.key_in (lines 15, 16, 24, 26, 36); k2-k9 and k1b-k8b are the same kind of link. Intermediate state: s0 (aes_128) stores, occurrence 2, CLOCKED_BY clk (line 11); state_in (one_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to s0 (line 77), and the entity recombines the looked-up words itself (lines 83-86); state_out (one_round) exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM z0 (line 88), exit ahead of storage; state_in (final_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to s0 (line 103), recombined at lines 109-112. Not realizing it: s0 of one_round and final_round (slices, DERIVES_FROM state_in at occurrence 2, lines 77 and 103), s1 and s9 of aes_128 (connections to r2.state_in and rf.state_in, lines 27 and 36; s2-s8 are the same), and table_lookup state, which only splits its word into b0-b3 (SOURCES, line 121) and hands them to T units (lines 123-126): 'An input used only for unchanged forwarding is not an eligible setting point'; S4 in and T in do the same. Finished block: state_out (final_round) exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM z0 (line 114); out (aes_128) exit port, occurrence 3, CONNECTS from rf.state_out (line 36); nothing only forwards or gates it between them. Under 'Do not treat every assignment as setting or every operator as computing a new conceptual value', the word terms v0-v3, k0a-k3a, k4a and k0b-k3b of expand_key_128 and z0-z3 of the rounds are parts of computations whose results are stored or leave at the references above, and table_lookup p0-p3 and the S4, T, S and xS outputs are lookup results inside the transformations: some are partners of cited edges, none is an additional reference.
7. Never reported. clk of aes_128, expand_key_128, one_round and final_round drives SEQUENCES (lines 9, 53, 61, 87, 113) and is wired to the sub-units' clk: a clock input, never a structural reference. The clk of every other module is likewise wired to its sub-units' clk (lines 123-126, 133-136, 143, 146) or sequences its case statement (lines 153, 417). The instance label rf and the formal rf.state_out are not on a PORT or SIGNAL line, so they are not candidates; the block leaves through out. The file has no reset, clock enable, record or transport port.
8. Checks. Each reference cites one of its own occurrence IDs and a record at that ID whose targets hold the partner, and the partner holds the mirror record; each edge fits its role: CLOCKED_BY for stores, a driving CARRIES or SOURCES on an input port of its own entity for sets, DERIVES_FROM or a connection from a sub-unit output for exit port. No element is reported on its name: k0 is declared in aes_128, expand_key_128, one_round and final_round, and s0 in aes_128, one_round and final_round, with different roles (stores in aes_128, forwarded words elsewhere); only the entity and the cited records separate them. Each concept rests on an integrity property with its lines; no confidentiality claim is made.

final_object.module purpose: aes_128 reads a 128-bit block (state) and a 128-bit key on each rising edge of clk, XORs them into s0 and keeps the key in k0 (lines 11-12), expands the key through ten expand_key_128 stages (lines 15-24), transforms the block through nine one_round stages and one final_round stage with the stage keys (lines 26-36), and drives the result on out.

use-case flows.value: initial mixing in aes_128: the input block XORed with the key, and the key itself, captured on the clock edge
key expansion in expand_key_128: the incoming stage key turned into the next stage's key (out_1, registered) and a round key (out_2)
one round in one_round: the block split, looked up, XORed with the round key and registered as the next block
final round in final_round: the block substituted, XORed with the last round key, registered, and driven out of aes_128
stage chaining in aes_128: each expansion stage's outputs feed the next stage and a round; each round's output feeds the next round

conceptual assets.concept: Cipher key material -- the secret key as it enters the core and as it is presented to the final round
conceptual assets.reasoning: Key capture, expansion and round mixing depend on the implemented key operands: `k0 <= key;` (line 12), `s0 <= state ^ key;` (line 11), `assign v0 = {k0[31:24] ^ rcon, k0[23:0]};` (line 49) and `assign k0b = k0a ^ k4a;` (line 57). Final mixing uses `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109); the other words follow their corresponding equations (lines 110-112). Corruption violates these transformation relations, establishing Integrity. Availability also applies to clocked key capture (line 12) and expansion-result production (line 62) on each rising edge of clk. The consumed key inputs are sets because each declaring entity reads them for storage or computation: key CARRIES to k0 (occurrence 4, line 12), in SOURCES k1 (occurrence 3, line 48), one_round key SOURCES k2 (occurrence 3, line 76), key_in SOURCES k3 (occurrence 3, line 102); each record targets all four words of its split, and one target is named. aes_128 k0 is stores, including its unchanged capture (CLOCKED_BY clk, occurrence 2, line 12). Expansion outputs are exit port through `out_1 <= {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` (line 62) and `assign out_2 = {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` (line 63), both DERIVES_FROM k0b, applying 'An output port through which the concept leaves its entity is an eligible exit' ahead of out_1's overlapping storage.

conceptual assets.concept: Intermediate cipher state -- the partially transformed block between rounds
conceptual assets.reasoning: The round-processing flow captures the initial transformed block with `s0 <= state ^ key;` (line 11, CLOCKED_BY clk at occurrence 2), performs lookup/XOR transformations including `assign z0 = p00 ^ p11 ^ p22 ^ p33 ^ k0;` (line 83), and registers the next block with `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` (line 88). Subsequent rounds depend on these particular results (s1-s9 connect each round to the next, lines 26-36), establishing Integrity. Availability independently applies to next-block production at each rising edge (lines 87-88), with matching lookup selectors. aes_128 s0 is stores, and one_round state_out is exit port ahead of its overlapping storage role (DERIVES_FROM z0, occurrence 3, line 88). Both round state_in ports are sets under 'an eligible input port is read by its declaring entity': after `assign {s0, s1, s2, s3} = state_in;` (SOURCES s0 at line 77, occurrence 3, and at line 103, occurrence 3), each entity invokes supplied transformations (lines 79-82, 105-108) and locally recombines their results, including final_round's `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109).

conceptual assets.concept: Ciphertext output -- the finished block leaving the core
conceptual assets.reasoning: The final flow forms the finished block using `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109) and the corresponding z1/z2/z3 equations (lines 110-112), then registers it with `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` (line 114, DERIVES_FROM z0 at occurrence 3). Integrity requires the reported block to agree with those final transformations. Availability independently applies to result production at rising edges (line 113) and delivery through `rf (clk, s9, k9b, out);` (line 36, the connection from rf.state_out at occurrence 3 of out), without assuming an external deadline. final_round state_out and aes_128 out are exit port because the block leaves their respective entities through them; 'An output port through which the concept leaves its entity is an eligible exit' applies, with exit taking precedence over state_out's storage role.
